parts.text: Choosing a preschool is a difficult and important decision. Parents are weighing cost, proximity and

with how each program meets the needs of the child and matches the goals and values of their family and cultural community.

This choice makes a difference. Research in early education clearly shows that children who attend high-quality preschool programs – those with smaller class sizes, a
appropriate curriculum, warm teacher-child interactions and established, efficient routines – are better prepared for

.

We are researchers who study early childhood education, and we conducted an 18-year study tracking the academic progress of 27,814 students who

different types of prekindergarten in Miami and then went on to attend the Miami-Dade County Public Schools system from kindergarten through high school. We found that the type of pre-K program the children attended made a difference for their overall educational

.

How we did our study

From 2002 to 2007, we partnered with Miami-Dade County Public Schools, early childcare providers across the county and the Early Learning Coalition of Miami-Dade, a nonprofit that works with childcare providers and communities to

school readiness, with the goal of assessing five cohorts of about 10,000 students per year.

School readiness takes into consideration the children’s cognitive, language,

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Regular park visits are associated with measurable differences in children's mental health.
Adults' responses to risk and mess can limit the benefits children gain from outdoor play.
A heavy burden of standardised testing does not necessarily lead to better learning.
A long-term study links public prekindergarten attendance to better later educational outcomes.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: We are researchers who study early childhood education, and we conducted an 18-year study tracking the academic progress of 27,814 students who attended different types of prekindergarten in Miami and then went on to attend the Miami-Dade County Public Schools system from kindergarten through high school.

questions.prompt: What does school readiness consider besides behaviour problems?
options: Only the price of a family's home
Cognitive, language, motor and social skills
Only a single mathematics score
Only whether children own a laptop
questions.explanation: 第 6 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: School readiness takes into consideration the children’s cognitive, language, motor and social skills, as well as behavior problems.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 12?
options: We believe that the answer likely lies in the quality and organizational differences between the three different types of early care and education.
It was just that the children in the public school preschools made stronger gains.
Kids who attended public school pre-K were 35% less likely to be held back in third grade compared with the other groups.
Further, we found that kids who attended higher-quality elementary schools – as measured by the Florida Department of Education – did better on average.
questions.explanation: 定位第 12 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Further, we found that kids who attended higher-quality elementary schools – as measured by the Florida Department of Education – did better on average.
